title: Primary display request transaction
summary: Readable C++ recovery of request-case2 at VA 0x4A1CD0, RVA 0xA1CD0, 1112 bytes including the fifteen-entry sample jump table. Original dispatcher case 2 at 0x4A1A6D forwards this and one request pointer; method returns bool in AL and pops four argument bytes. Six exact comparisons permit a flag-only fast path. Changed requests release resources, optionally save window coordinates, reset D3D presentation parameters, resize resources, and restore. Initial reset failure restores presentation parameters and calls window-mode adjustment with requested dimensions but old fullscreen byte. Restoration failure resets the saved parameters, ignores that reset result, resizes using parameters reloaded after reset, and restores only the six saved settings. Successful commit stores the raw fullscreen/sample settings, calculates unsigned-to-float dimension ratios, updates viewport, copies the request flag and invokes the refresh/timing helper. Side effects of external callbacks are preserved, including partial rollback and delayed snapshots. Accepted assembly was checked against direct immutable executable disassembly and all 1112 relocated reference bytes compared equal. No compiler byte match is claimed.
test_description: Completed a local fixed-address GCC i386 freestanding link with accepted request_case2.S at 0x4A1CD0, cookie_check.S at 0x8F8958 and the provided test runtime. The C++ boundary doubles and original data locations are mapped by /out/check.ld; mapping addresses are also documented in test.cpp. 50376 direct original-reference differential cases passed at fixed GCC O0 flags, and again with implementation compiled as C++11 at O2. Covers unchanged input, each of six independent differences, success, negative initial reset, restoration failure with ignored negative or positive rollback reset, sample values 0 through 17 plus 0x80000000 and 0xFFFFFFFF, raw mode bytes 0/1/2/255, eleven dimension values from zero through unsigned extremes, and all four masked MXCSR rounding modes. Compares return, whole guarded 0xBAC-byte display storage, complete request and window bytes, every callback's ordered arguments and full state snapshot, and final MXCSR including exception flags. An independent ordinary-path footprint/sequence check verifies untouched fields and guards. All 127 combinations of seven mutating callback behaviors exercise delayed loads, snapshot timing, reset modifications, request mutation and persistent unrelated side effects. 336 cases additionally use the implementation's original-address defaults, including the indirect GetWindowRect IAT adapter. An unmapped default link was run separately: it prints LIMIT and runs 50040 portable assertions without claiming original differential coverage.
known_limits: Only the assigned routine is recovered. Resource release 0x4A6330, restoration 0x4A6560, resource-size update 0x53D2D0, window-mode update 0x48CB30, viewport 0x4A22E0, refresh/timing update 0x4A5B00 and GetWindowRect remain external boundaries. Tests substitute observing and mutating ordinary C++ doubles for those dependencies, rather than validating D3D or Win32 implementations.

The full differential suite requires the fixed section mappings documented in test.cpp and exercised by the local check.ld link. A trusted default link that does not position these sections prints an explicit LIMIT and performs portable checks only; it must not be reported as a full original comparison.

GetWindowRect's return value is ignored by the original. Tests cover a false return with a fully written rectangle. A failure leaving rectangle bytes uninitialized depends on original stack contents and has no deterministic high-level contract; the implementation intentionally does not invent fallback coordinates.

Object/request fields without firm semantic identification retain offset-based names. source274 and saved274 are deliberately not assigned stronger meaning. The modeled opaque object extent is 0xBAC bytes based on caller-visible fields, not recovered debug type information.

Valid non-overlapping objects and request storage, a live device/vtable, compatible callbacks and initialized singleton slots are required. Invalid pointers, concurrent mutation, reentrant target invocation and aliasing between request/object/presentation storage are not tested. Boundary rebinding is intended for port integration and tests, not concurrent use.

FP tests use masked exceptions with default DAZ/FTZ. Zero denominators, zero-over-zero, large unsigned conversion rounding and MXCSR flags are compared, but unmasked traps and alternate FP hardware environments are untested.

Pinned /tools/msvc/msvc is absent in this sandbox. Implementation compiles with GCC as C++11 and uses fixed-width types, a genuine thiscall member method, and guarded MSVC ABI declarations; native MSVC2013 compilation remains for the coordinator. No matching-source byte credit or complete-game portability is claimed.
